paragraphs: Art. 1. (1) Ownership is restored of the real estate expropriated under the Act on the Expropriation of Large Urban Covered Real Estate (1948) that is owned by the state, the municipalities, public organisations or their firms or the single-owner companies under Art. 61 of the Commerce Act, and exists in reality up to the size in which it was expropriated.

(2) Transactions made in breach of the decision of the Grand National Assembly of 6 December 1990 on the partial lifting of the ban on the disposal of state and municipal property are void, and the ownership of the properties transferred is restored.

Art. 2. (1) Ownership is restored of the properties expropriated under: the State Tobacco Monopoly Act; the State Monopoly of Petroleum Products Act; the Monopoly of Spirits, Sweetened Spirit Drinks and Trade in Fruit Brandies and Wine Act; the Nationalisation of Private Industrial and Mining Enterprises Act; the Cinematography Act; the Printing Act; the Decree on the Expropriation of Food Storehouses; the State Insurance Institute Act; the Banks Act; the acts on the purchase of large agricultural equipment, of large agricultural machinery and of commercial equipment; the Nationalisation of Cargo Vessels Act; the Decree on Mines and Underground Resources; and of the properties confiscated under the Ordinance-Act on the trial by the People's Court, the Act on the Confiscation of Property Acquired by Speculation or Unlawfully, Art. 56 of the Ordinance-Act on Supply and Prices, Art. 17 of the Act on the Collection of Taxes and Other State Receivables and the Ordinance on the Collection of Taxes and Fees, and under the decrees by which property of citizens was taken in favour of the state. [The State Gazette references of the listed acts are omitted.]

(1a) Every person whose property was confiscated under the Act on the Confiscation of Property Acquired by Speculation or Unlawfully and under Art. 56 of the Ordinance-Act on Supply and Prices, and that person's successors, may propose a review of the sentences by which the property was confiscated, under chapter eighteen of the Criminal Procedure Code, within the term under Art. 6(1).

(2) Ownership is also restored of all movable and immovable property taken without a legal ground, or expropriated outside the procedure set by law, by the state, the municipalities and the people's councils in the period from 9 September 1944 to 1989.

(3) Ownership of the properties under para. 1 is restored if, when this act entered into force, they were owned by the state, the municipalities, public organisations or their firms or the single-owner companies under Art. 61 of the Commerce Act, and if they exist in reality up to the size in which they were expropriated.

Art. 3. (1) Ownership of the properties under Art. 1 and 2 is restored to the persons from whom they were taken, or to their legal heirs or other successors. The right to the restitution is established by the fact that the ownership was taken from them or from their predecessors. Claims of third persons to rights in the same properties do not prevent the restitution to the persons from whom the properties were taken. Disputes between the claimants are settled between them by a claim.

(2) Ownership is restored to all legal entities, churches, monasteries, mosques, synagogues and other religious communities, community centres and schools whose properties were expropriated as described in Art. 1 and Art. 2(1) and (2). When the legal entities do not exist when this act enters into force, the ownership is restored to their partners or members, or to the natural persons who were their members or partners when they ended, according to the rights of each of them or of their legal heirs.
(3) When the conditions for restitution of the properties under Art. 1 and 2 are not met, their former owners or their heirs are compensated in the procedure of a separate act.

Art. 4. (1) Ownership of the properties under Art. 1 and 2 is restored if the owners were not compensated by payment of their money value or with another equivalent real estate. Receiving bonds does not count as compensation.

(2) Persons for whom a set-off was made under the Decree on the set-off of the obligations of former owners of properties expropriated by the state and of nationalised enterprises to the state, the banks and the state enterprises (1955) are not deemed compensated.

(3) The owners of properties under Art. 8 of the Act on the Expropriation of Large Urban Covered Real Estate and Art. 7 of the Nationalisation of Private Industrial and Mining Enterprises Act who received dwellings as compensation or in exchange may request the restitution. The request is made not later than 6 months from the entry into force of this act to the Minister of Finance, who decides within 30 days; silence counts as a tacit refusal. Refusals are appealed within 14 days before the Supreme Court, which decides the dispute on the merits. The Administrative Procedure Code applies to matters not regulated.

(4) When the decision under para. 3 enters into force, the real estate given as compensation or in exchange becomes state or municipal property and is taken back under Art. 16 of the Property Act. It cannot be taken back before 6 months from the decision on restitution, and in the cases of Art. 6(2), before the three-year term expires.
Art. 5. (1) The heirs of the persons to whom the ownership of the properties under Art. 1 and 2 is restored are exempt from the inheritance tax.

(2) The acquisitive prescription that ran for properties whose ownership is restored under this act, under the Ownership and Use of Agricultural Land Act or under the Act on Amnesty and Return of Taken Property is not counted, and starts to run from the day this provision enters into force.
